Sunday June 14, 2026 morning. The June 14 morning brief opens in the most consequential deal-signing liminal state of the 107-day Hormuz conflict arc. On the evening of June 13, President Trump posted on Truth Social that the US-Iran deal is 'scheduled to get signed tomorrow' — June 14 — and that 'immediately after it is signed, the Hormuz Strait is OPEN TO ALL.' This is the first specific presidential signing-date commitment of the conflict: a named date, not 'soon' or 'over the weekend.' The Qatari mediators flew to Tehran in the early morning hours of June 14 to complete final text reconciliation, with Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner conducting multiple phone calls with the Qatari envoy. The MOU terms as now confirmed by Axios (June 12) and NBC News differ materially from the prior 30-day reopening framework: Iran commits to opening the Strait of Hormuz immediately upon signing — not within 30 days — and the US commits to releasing $25 billion in frozen assets while waiving oil sanctions simultaneously. The immediate Hormuz reopening language removes the 30-day energy-market uncertainty window entirely and accelerates the deflationary relief timeline from weeks to hours. Against this: Iranian FM spokesman Baqaei issued a June 13 hedge that a June 14 signing is 'unlikely' but 'could happen in the coming days.' Brent closed Friday at ~$86.5 — down 4%+ on the week, the lowest since early March — confirming markets have pre-priced 60-70% deal probability. FOMC T-2 carries a newly identified complexity: the June 16-17 Warsh meeting is a Summary of Economic Projections (SEP) meeting, releasing the dot plot alongside the rate decision. If the deal signs today and Brent drops $5-8 immediately, Warsh's dot plot energy-CPI assumptions may be partially obsolete by the time he delivers his June 17 press conference — making this the most anomalous inaugural SEP context in recent Fed history. PNW situational awareness is at maximum operational stress: Extreme Heat Warning Day 1 is active (92-100°F), the FIFA opener is T-1 under peak heat (Belgium vs Egypt, June 15 noon PT, Lumen Field; AccuWeather flags potential Seattle June 15 all-time temperature record), BLM statewide fire restrictions are operative across both states, and the Frontage Fire near Huntington, OR (I-84 corridor, 1,000 acres, partially contained) is the first named fire of the east Oregon heat-accelerated season.

items.summary: The June 14 morning brief opens at the most consequential deal-signing window of the 107-day Hormuz conflict arc. On June 13 evening, President Trump posted on Truth Social that the deal is 'scheduled to get signed tomorrow' — naming June 14 by date — and stated that 'immediately after it is signed, the Hormuz Strait is OPEN TO ALL.' This is the first specific presidential signing-date commitment of the conflict arc: not a generic 'soon' or 'weekend,' but a named calendar date. Qatari mediators flew to Tehran in the early morning hours of June 14 to complete final text reconciliation; Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner conducted multiple phone calls with the Qatari envoy during the Tehran session. The Qatari channel is a new addition to the mediation architecture alongside the Pakistani PM Sharif channel and signals the Gulf diplomatic network has fully mobilized for closing. MOU terms now confirmed by Axios (June 12) and NBC News are materially more favorable than the prior 30-day framework: (1) Iran commits to opening the Strait of Hormuz IMMEDIATELY upon signing — not within 30 days; this change removes the 30-day energy-market uncertainty window and accelerates the deflationary relief timeline from weeks to hours post-signing; (2) US commits to releasing $25 billion in frozen Iranian assets, including via direct cash transfers; (3) US commits to waiving existing oil sanctions on Tehran immediately and imposing no new sanctions until a final deal is reached; (4) Iran commits to neither producing nor purchasing nuclear weapons; (5) Iran commits to diluting its highly enriched uranium stockpile in-country; (6) Iran commits to no new uranium enrichment until a final deal is concluded; (7) 60-day follow-on nuclear negotiation window. Against this: Iranian FM spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei issued a June 13 hedge that the signing is 'unlikely on June 14' but 'could happen in the coming days' — consistent with Iranian diplomatic pattern of publicly hedging against externally announced timelines. Iranian state media has played down the June 14 probability. This hedge is assessed as a counterpart communication pattern, not a deal-collapse signal; the signing could legitimately occur June 15-16 even if June 14 slips. Iran comms resolved streak advances to Day 11 — longest confirmed-open channel streak of the conflict arc. Beirut-suburbs partial truce Day 12 clean. Lebanon ceasefire Day 29. CENTCOM has issued no stand-down order; Hormuz closed Day 107; kinetic posture active-but-paused pending deal confirmation.

items.headline: FOMC T-2 — SEP/Dot Plot Meeting: Full Rate Path Projection Through 2028; Deal Signing Could Render Energy-CPI Assumptions Obsolete Within 48 Hours of Dot Plot Finalization; Warsh First Press Conference June 17; Hold 97% Certain; Brent Deflationary Signal Accelerating
items.summary: The June 14 morning economic brief is defined by the convergence of two interdependent signals: the deal-signing window (Brent already ~$86.5, down 4%+ on the week) and the FOMC T-2 countdown — newly confirmed as a Summary of Economic Projections (SEP) meeting. The SEP designation materially elevates the June 16-17 meeting's significance beyond a statement-bias shift: the Committee will release the updated dot plot alongside the rate decision, showing individual member rate path projections through 2028. The rate decision itself is near-certain (97% hold probability per Polymarket; 3% hike). The primary market signal is the dot plot's answer to three questions: (1) Do FOMC members project any 2026 rate hike? The April meeting produced 4 dissents — most divided since 1992 — suggesting a meaningful faction views May CPI 4.2% YoY and nominal spending 5.9% QoQ annualized as requiring tighter policy; (2) Does the first rate cut get projected in 2026 (September window) or pushed to 2027? (3) Do projections assume the energy CPI channel (~40% YoY gasoline contribution to headline) resolves or persists? The extraordinary complication: if Trump signs the Iran deal today (June 14) and Brent drops toward $80-84 immediately on sanctions waiver and immediate Hormuz reopening, the dot plot finalized for June 17 release may be partially obsolete on its single largest CPI driver within 48 hours of the Committee's finalization. A 40%+ YoY gasoline shock that begins resolving hours before the dot plot is published would produce the most anomalous SEP energy-projection context of any Fed meeting in recent memory. Warsh's June 17 press conference must credibly address both the dot plot's rate path and a potentially rapidly-resolving supply shock in real time — his inaugural chair-defining event now has an additional layer of deal-timing complexity. ECB hike signal remains active as external monetary pressure. MOU oil sanctions waiver = Iran supply re-entry into global markets = structural Brent ceiling removal = largest single deflationary CPI impulse available in 2026.

items.summary: Four secondary infrastructure threads entering June 14 morning. First: NSF Newport OR ocean observatory is still operational and contributing to the June 14-16 Extreme Heat Warning forecast modeling — this is precisely the capability set being lost. The observatory's Pacific Ocean surface temperature, atmospheric pressure, and marine atmospheric data feed NWS Portland's modeling suite; the June 14-16 event is forecast with the station active, but the observatory will be removed in approximately two weeks (~June 28-30), and the next major heat or atmospheric river event entering the PNW will be forecast without it. This event is the last major atmospheric event Newport's sensors will capture; its operational presence through June 14-16 is a final illustration of the monitoring capacity about to disappear. Second: Longview, Washington CSB unstable chemical storage tank Day 20 — 90,000 gallons of hazardous material in a structurally compromised tank. The June 14-16 heat wave introduces an elevated vapor pressure concern for the Longview facility: elevated ambient temperatures increase internal pressure in liquid-chemical storage systems. No resolution announcement or incident in the overnight cycle, but the heat-wave + chemical storage co-occurrence is a watch item through the June 14-16 window. items.summary: The primary PNW civic thread entering June 14 morning is the arrival of the Extreme Heat Warning (Day 1) coinciding with the final 29 hours before the FIFA Seattle opener (Belgium vs Egypt, June 15, noon PT, Lumen Field). Sunday is the heat ramp phase — 90-94°F in Portland and Seattle — with the peak (95-100°F) arriving Monday, directly overlapping the noon PT kickoff. AccuWeather's World Cup weather tracker flags that June 15 temperatures could threaten Seattle's all-time high for that calendar date, making tomorrow potentially both the city's hottest June 15 on record and the day of its most-attended international sporting event. The match opens under SEAR-2 security posture with $32M FEMA grant, CCTV operational (Day 4), and drone restrictions active around Lumen Field. Lumen Field's upper deck partial shade provides limited relief at noon peak solar radiation; the open pitch and direct-sun seating areas present elevated heat-related medical emergency risk at SEAR-2 crowd density. Egypt carries a potential weather advantage — native June climate in the 30s Celsius vs Belgium's typical 21°C June highs — which may affect match performance alongside crowd public health. Let's Play SEA 26 enters Day 4 at Seattle Center — an open-air fan zone with no air conditioning; cooling center protocols, hydration distribution, and heat-related incident monitoring are the primary watch items. Multnomah County and Portland cooling centers are activating Sunday morning per the 2021 heat dome (1,000+ Oregon deaths) response protocol; no heat-related mortality reported in the overnight cycle. CISA clean streak advances to Day 43; Shamkhani IRGC cyber risk Day 20 — no confirmed venue network incident or FBI IC3 flash in overnight cycle. NIFC-FIFA co-response Day 7: BLM statewide fire restrictions active; Frontage Fire (Huntington, OR, I-84 corridor) partially contained; any new east Oregon or Columbia Gorge ignition under Sunday heat conditions immediately tests co-response resource allocation. Sound Transit $34.5B funding gap T-1 — Link Light Rail primary Lumen Field transit mode with no board capital resolution confirmed.

items.headline: NIFC Above-Normal Day 14 — BLM Fire Restrictions Active; Oregon 83% Drought; Washington Drought Day 10 (4th Year); NSF Newport OR Active For This Event — Dark Before Next; Oregon Gray Whale 21 YTD
items.summary: Four secondary PNW environmental threads entering June 14 morning. First: NIFC above-normal Day 14 with BLM statewide fire restrictions active across Oregon and Washington — the first formal federal restriction level of the 2026 season. Capital Press confirmed June 4 that 'the risk period for big Western fires is arriving early,' consistent with drought-year-4 conditions and below-normal snowpack. The Frontage Fire (Huntington, OR, approximately 1,000 acres, started June 6, Level 3 evacuations reduced) is the first named fire of the east Oregon season; the I-84 corridor it burned is also a FIFA security and transit route. Heat accelerates fuel drying: the June 14-16 window (90-100°F) with 50%-of-normal Washington snowpack and 83% Oregon drought coverage is the highest combined ignition-risk window since NIFC above-normal Day 1; east Cascades are explicitly above-normal in the June NIFC outlook; fire onset target of July is T-16 days and the heat window may accelerate that timeline. Second: NSF Newport OR ocean observatory is still operational and contributing to the June 14-16 forecast — this event is the last major atmospheric system the station will capture before its end-of-June removal. In approximately two weeks, the station goes dark; the next major heat event or atmospheric river entering the PNW will be forecast without it. The June 14-16 brief is a live illustration of the monitoring capability about to disappear. Third: Oregon gray whale washups continue at 21 YTD (Oregon coast), 17 YTD (Washington) — above expected annual pace; serious emaciation consistent with Pacific prey availability collapse; the ocean monitoring network dismantlement (Newport removal ~2 weeks) runs concurrent with a marine ecosystem stress signal that requires exactly the monitoring capacity being eliminated. Fourth: Washington drought emergency Day 10 (4th consecutive year); Oregon 83% coverage (12 counties emergency); Washington snowpack approximately 50% of normal; El Nino 61% / Super El Nino 1-in-4; soil moisture deficit advancing under heat.

analyst_summary: June 14, 2026 morning opens at Vibe 4 upper edge — held by three incomplete states, but functioning primarily as the opening brief of the highest-stakes single-day deal window of the 107-day conflict arc. Trump named June 14 on Truth Social. Qatari mediators are in Tehran. Witkoff and Kushner are on the phones. Brent closed Friday at $86.5 — the lowest since early March — confirming markets have pre-priced 60-70% deal probability. The MOU terms now confirmed (Axios/NBC) are more favorable than the prior DVC framework tracked: Hormuz reopening upon signing is immediate, not 30-day; US releases $25B and waives oil sanctions simultaneously. A confirmed deal today triggers an unconditional Vibe 5 upgrade: immediate Hormuz reopening, oil sanctions waived, Iran supply re-entry, gasoline price relief beginning within days, WPA constitutional clock rendered moot, House Republican midterm exposure ends, Reconciliation 2.0 political lubricant activated, and the FOMC dot plot's energy-CPI assumptions become obsolete in the most consequential way possible — by resolution, not persistence. Four structural risk factors sustain the 4 ceiling through brief generation: (1) deal unsigned — Iranian FM Baqaei hedge 'unlikely June 14 but coming days'; 107-day arc contains five prior false-close cycles; Trump final-edit and Khamenei authorization unconfirmed; (2) PNW heat-fire-FIFA triple convergence at Day 1 maximum stress — Extreme Heat Warning active (90-100°F through Tuesday), FIFA opener T-1 under peak heat advisory with potential Seattle June 15 all-time high, NIFC-FIFA co-response Day 7 with BLM statewide fire restrictions and Frontage Fire I-84 partially contained; (3) FOMC T-2 SEP/dot plot — the full rate path projection adds complexity beyond the statement shift; 4 April dissents; energy-CPI assumptions potentially made obsolete within 48 hours of finalization by a deal signing today; Warsh inaugural press conference carries dual mandate (define chair voice + address potentially resolving supply shock in real time); (4) Measles 2,073 — CIDRAP slowing signal Day 7 is the strongest deceleration indicator of the outbreak but is fragile under the FIFA-heat June 15 amplification scenario (highest single-day measles transmission risk of the year). Primary watch items: (1) deal signing or delay signal — monitor Brent as fastest proxy; $80-84 = signed; $90+ = delay or collapse; (2) overnight east Cascades ignitions entering Sunday morning; (3) FIFA June 15 pre-match public health preparation under heat advisory; (4) Warsh dot plot preparation signal — any pre-meeting Fed communication in the Sunday blackout window; (5) measles FIFA-heat amplification monitoring June 15.
